report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of graph_delta.py: measure/run/render/main/held_out plus helper functions; verified claims about in-memory application, conservative one-file measurement, clean/leaky arms, and reproducibility comments.
risks: line ~214 | medium | _ast_refs may fail on parse errors: if err_b or err_a, skipped_reason set but layers still appended; detection could be based on partially computed refs. | Confirm whether skipped_reason prevents detection downstream.

line ~217 | medium | _type_edge_keys catches AttributeError and SyntaxError but not other exceptions (e.g., TypeError from malformed AST facts); could crash measure. | Check parse_mod.python_type_facts for other exception paths.

line ~216 | medium | The 'data.literals' layer is silently skipped on ImportError; a missing structcore dependency would degrade the report without notice. | Verify structcore is always available in the environment.

line ~150 | low | _structure_by_function uses depth > 24 guard; deeply nested code beyond depth 24 is ignored, potentially undercounting structure changes. | Confirm depth limits match mutation expectations.
line ~211 | low | measure uses target.read_text without specifying encoding; default locale-dependent encoding may cause inconsistent results across platforms. | Confirm files are always UTF-8.
line ~230 | low | run() sorts by_class dict; the order is deterministic but not specified in any contract. | No issue unless external consumers depend on order.

line ~246 | low | render() uses fixed-width formatting ('44', '32', '>6') that may truncate long mutation IDs or class names; not a correctness issue but could hide information. | Check if truncation is acceptable.
line ~253 | low | main() writes output files unconditionally; if a run fails midway, a partial JSON file may be left behind. | Confirm error handling in main.

line ~260 | medium | held_out() is defined but its body is not in this chunk (ends at generate import); the docstring claims 'MECHANICALLY generated corpus' and 'no knowledge of scoring layers' but these are uncheckable here. | Inspect mutate.generate and held_out body.

line ~257 | medium | main() comment claims specificity, commit_shas, and measure_commit are defined below the if __name__ block, but those names are listed as defined elsewhere in this file; the comment's claim about 'no committed command' is uncheckable without seeing the rest of the file. | Verify the placement of those definitions.

handoff.purpose: Measure mutation effects on graph layers, run the corpus, render results, and provide CLI entry points.

symbols.name: _structure_by_function
symbols.note: Parses text, walks AST, counts node class names at depths for each function body, excluding names and constants; returns dict of function name to Counter.

symbols.name: _structure_keys
symbols.note: Builds a set of keys like 'fn:Stmt@depth#i' from _structure_by_function output.

symbols.name: _units_and_refs
symbols.note: Extracts units via parse_mod.extract_units and collects identifier references as 'unit->name' strings; returns tuple (units, refs).

symbols.name: _type_edge_keys
symbols.note: Extracts type facts, produces keys for types, fields, consumes, produces; returns empty set on AttributeError or SyntaxError.

symbols.name: measure
symbols.note: Applies a mutation in memory (read/replace), computes five layers (leaky refs, AST refs, literals, structure, types) plus optional data.literals, returns DeltaResult.

symbols.name: run
symbols.note: Loads mutations, measures each, aggregates by defect class, returns summary dict with skipped/detected/missed.

symbols.name: render
symbols.note: Formats the run report as a human-readable string table.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry: handles --held-out, --specificity, default run; writes JSON evidence files to runs/eval/.

symbols.name: held_out
symbols.note: Docstring describes held-out evaluation over mechanically generated corpus; body not fully shown (only the start).

claims.text: moves the reference layer and not this one, and a change that wraps a statement in ``if not ...`` moves this one and not the others.
claims.why: The function records only node class names and depths; it does not record names or constants, and wrapping a statement in if not would change the node class at depth 0, so the claim is consistent with the implementation.
The depth check stops recursion at depth 24, preventing runaway traversal on deeply nested or adversarial input.

claims.text: Names and constants are the OTHER layers' business. Recording only the node class is what keeps the three signals independent.
claims.why: The code explicitly skips ast.Name, ast.Constant, ast.Load, ast.Store, ast.Del, so only node classes are counted, preserving independence.

claims.text: Per-unit identifier references — the name-based call view, one file wide.
claims.why: The function uses parse_mod.extract_units on a single file and collects identifiers from each unit's source.

claims.text: Whole-repo resolution is deliberately not used: the question is whether the graph MOVES, and a single file answers that far more cheaply than two index builds.
claims.why: The function only processes the given module text; no cross-file resolution is performed.

claims.text: A cross-file consequence would only ADD movement, so measuring one file is the conservative direction.
claims.why: Since the function only looks at one file, any cross-file effects are ignored, which means movement can only be undercounted, not overcounted.

claims.text: Type-layer edges for one file, as comparable keys.
claims.why: The function extracts type facts from the given module text and builds keys from those facts.

claims.text: Uses the same extraction the index uses.
claims.why: The chunk does not show what the index uses; parse_mod.python_type_facts is referenced but its equivalence to the index is not verifiable here.

claims.text: Degrades to an empty set for a language with no type vocabulary — which is reported, never silently treated as 'nothing changed'.
claims.why: The function returns an empty set on AttributeError/SyntaxError, but the claim about 'reported' depends on how the caller (measure) handles the empty set; measure appends a LayerDelta with empty added/removed, which may be treated as 'moved' false, but the docstring's 'reported' is not fully demonstrated.

claims.text: Apply one mutation IN MEMORY and report what moved. Nothing is written.
claims.why: measure reads the file, does a string replace, and computes layers; it never writes to disk. The only side effects are in-memory computations.

claims.text: The corpus is pinned to a revision; a drifted anchor is a real finding about the corpus, not a licence to fuzzy-match into place.
claims.why: If mutation.find is not in before, measure sets skipped_reason and returns without applying, refusing to fuzzy-match.

claims.text: LEAKY arm: raw-source identifiers, comments included. Kept on purpose -- the gap between the two arms IS the measured size of the marker artefact.
claims.why: The leaky arm uses _units_and_refs which uses parse_mod.extract_units; whether comments are included depends on extract_units, but the claim is that comments count. The code does not strip comments, so the claim is consistent with the implementation.

claims.text: CLEAN arm: AST identifiers. Comments are not tokens here.
claims.why: _ast_refs parses the source with ast.parse, which ignores comments; so comments are not included.

claims.text: Skipped mutants are NOT counted as misses and NOT counted as passes. An anchor that no longer matches means the corpus drifted; folding that into either column would turn a bookkeeping problem into a result.
claims.why: run() excludes skipped mutants from applied, detected, and missed; skipped are listed separately in the output.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30: `specificity`, `commit_shas` and `measure_commit` are defined BELOW the `if __name__` block and this function is defined above them, so no committed command could reach the specificity arm at all. The published false-alarm figures (0.9% refs, 0.7% structure) were produced by a throwaway script during a session and could not be regenerated by anyone afterwards -- a measurement without a command is a measurement without provenance, which this repository treats as no measurement.
claims.why: The claim about the placement of those definitions and the lack of a committed command cannot be verified from this chunk alone; the names are listed as defined elsewhere in the file, but their exact line positions and the absence of a command are not observable here.

claims.text: Detection rate over a MECHANICALLY generated corpus, per operator.
claims.why: The body of held_out is not fully shown; only the docstring and the import of mutate.generate are visible.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30, and the reason this exists as a function rather than as a number in a document: the published 75.3% held-out figure had **no committed command**. ... This repository treats a measurement without a command as a measurement without provenance, which is to say as no measurement at all.
claims.why: The claim about the historical measurement and the lack of a committed command cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: Held out in the meaningful sense: :mod:`daedalus.eval.mutate` builds the corpus from the tree by rule, with no knowledge of what the scoring layers look at, so nothing here was tuned against these specific mutants.
claims.why: The mutation generation logic is in mutate.generate, not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Scored on the CLEAN arm only. The three layers are applied to a function's source before and after mutation, and a mutant counts as detected if any of them moves. Per-operator breakdown is reported because the aggregate hides the interesting failure -- one operator scoring zero while the rest score well is a blind spot, and it averages away into a respectable-looking total.
claims.why: The actual scoring logic is in the held_out function body, which is not shown in this chunk.

observations.what: measure() sets skipped_reason on AST parse errors but still appends the 'code.refs.ast' layer with possibly empty/partial sets; detection may be affected.
The 'data.literals' layer is silently skipped on ImportError, which could hide a dependency problem.
_type_edge_keys catches only AttributeError and SyntaxError; other exceptions could propagate and abort the whole run.
main() writes JSON output files without any error handling; a failure during serialization or writing could leave partial files.
The held_out function is only partially shown; its docstring makes strong claims about methodology that cannot be verified from this chunk.
